nodes.title: Home Assistant Floor Plan Requirements
widgets_values:
For Home Assistant floor plans, you need an SVG file, not a PNG/JPG.

Key Requirements:
1. SVG element `id` must match HA entity names (e.g., `binary_sensor.living_room`)
2. Each zone needs its own SVG path/rect element
3. Use vector elements: `<path>`, `<rect>`, `<circle>`
4. No transforms on elements (or they need to be wrapped in `<g>`)

Example SVG Structure:
```svg
<svg width="1024" height="1024">
  <rect id="binary_sensor.living_room" x="100" y="100" width="300" height="200" fill="#7cb1f9"/>
  <path id="light.kitchen" d="M400,400 L500,400 L500,500 L400,500 Z" fill="white"/>
</svg>
```

For this workflow, consider:
1. Generate the static floor plan image (done)
2. Extract room boundaries as SVG paths
3. Add HA entity IDs to each zone
4. Create the CSS styling for state changes

nodes.title: Next Steps
widgets_values:
To create a HA-compatible floor plan:

1. Generate your floor plan image (this workflow)
2. Open in vector editor (Inkscape, Illustrator, or online SVG editor)
3. Trace each room zone and assign entity IDs
4. Create HA entity IDs matching your sensors:
   - binary_sensor.living_room
   - binary_sensor.kitchen
   - binary_sensor.garage
   - binary_sensor.pool
   - binary_sensor.backyard
   - light.main_lights
   - switch.fan
5. Add CSS for state-based styling (on/off colors)
6. Save as .svg and place in HA www/floorplan/ directory

Or manually create the SVG using:
- Inkscape (free): https://inkscape.org
- SVG Editor (online): https://svg-editor.fosscommunity.org
- VS Code + SVG extensions
